status: Research complete; small adaptation proposed, no skill created or installed
request: Review handoff sources across all 19 repositories carried forward from the user-supplied corpus, beyond named skills; reassess direct adoption versus adaptation with a tool-agnostic design and OS temporary storage accepted.

scope.method: SSH acquisition at the recorded branch tips; complete tracked-path inventories; repository-wide text screening of md, mdx, mdc, rst, txt and license files including hidden directories; selected full reads and explicitly bounded excerpts, plus targeted source-code cross-checks.
limits: This is not a line-by-line audit of all 43,935 paths or all 1,375 matched files.
Translations, host mirrors and fixtures contribute to counts and are not independent sources.
No donor workflow, lifecycle hook or handoff skill was executed, installed or behaviorally evaluated.

correction.previous: The atlas treated OS temporary storage versus .tmp and the local Orca transfer protocol as reasons to adapt Matt handoff.
correction.finding: That rationale conflates artifact content with execution transfer. The user accepts OS temporary storage, and generic instructions should not depend on a named host.
correction.storage: OS temporary storage and checkout .tmp are both valid when the intended recipient can access the file and its dependencies for the needed lifetime. For another filesystem or longer retention, choose an appropriate accessible destination without inventing transport authorization.

recommendation.rationale: Matt is adequate as a manually invoked summary exporter. Strict tool independence requires only replacing the literal Skill tool reference with portable wording. A few additional continuation and evidence decisions would improve usefulness; they are proposed quality improvements, not compatibility requirements. Several already appear in its companion guide. No combined handoff system is justified.
essentialContent: Current objective and relevant scope or authorization, with user decisions distinguished from agent inference.
Actual done, partial and pending state; relevant repository/revision and dirty state only when useful.
Next useful action and why; blockers, failed approaches and traps only when they affect continuation.
Applicable verification evidence and remaining acceptance checks; an unrun check is not a pass.
Pointers to existing artifacts with what matters there, whether the receiver can access them, and any material lifetime limitation.
recommendation.boundary: Produce a usable artifact and its location. Creation, receipt and transfer of execution are distinct outcomes. The core does not launch sessions, move worktrees, commit, push, cancel agents or impose a host-specific protocol.
recommendation.proportionality: Use the smallest task-appropriate structure. No obligatory Git section for non-code work, no fixed context threshold, no managed history database, and no fresh session required for an ordinary phase transition.
alternatives: Direct adoption is reasonable if the need is only a short manually requested export and the caller supplies the missing continuation details.
Compound is the fuller option only if indexed discovery and an explicit orientation-before-action workflow become a real requirement.
No new skill is needed when the receiving agent already has adequate durable context through the host.

A separate background-Claude launcher, not the portable document capability.

candidates.title: Matt Pocock · handoff
candidates.does: Writes a short, focused conversation export with artifact references and suggested skills.
candidates.keep: Keep its small scope, references instead of copied plans, sensitive-data redaction and ability to hand off a side task while the original conversation continues.
candidates.change: Use portable skill-loading language and make continuation state, evidence, decision provenance and accessible references explicit in the loaded instructions. Codex metadata already exists.

candidates.title: Compound Engineering · ce-handoff
candidates.role: Source of selected creation and resume safeguards
candidates.does: Creates a continuity document, discovers saved handoffs and orients a new session from an explicitly selected source.
candidates.keep: Annotate pointers with what matters, distinguish completed and pending work, preserve user intent versus agent inference, check current state and avoid overwriting another artifact.
candidates.change: A managed store, indexed discovery and compulsory confirmation after every resume exceed the requested export capability. Respect a present request to continue; an old document alone does not authorize new work.

candidates.title: Allen Eubank · agent-profile handoff
candidates.does: Captures task state for another agent, with the next action first and explicit acceptance and decisions.
candidates.keep: Put the useful next step up front; preserve acceptance evidence and whether decisions were confirmed or still provisional.
candidates.change: Do not require ~/.handoffs, a coordinator charter, a hunk sidecar or a fresh session after every ship/pivot/wait event. Git details are conditional on the task.

candidates.title: GSD · handoff and guided resume
candidates.does: Checkpoints active work inside its milestone/task system and recovers it through continuation artifacts.
candidates.keep: Record the next action and its reason, partial outputs, useful failed attempts and traps. A cold reader should know how to continue. Keep needed recovery material until superseded or complete.
candidates.change: Leave .gsd paths, GSD task tools, state regeneration and background-job control with their existing owners. Its workflow and guided-resume prompt disagree about deleting the recovery document, another reason not to import that lifecycle wholesale.

candidates.title: Lauren Tan · pstack pause and pickup
candidates.does: Stops explicitly requested work at a resumable boundary and reconstructs a resume point from the prior trail and current artifacts.
candidates.keep: Carry the actual resume point, known verification and links to existing evidence; avoid repeating completed investigation.
candidates.change: Writing a handoff does not imply a pause, automatic WIP commit or nested-agent cancellation. Reconcile inherited claims with relevant current artifacts rather than trusting a self-report or restarting everything.

candidates.title: Addy Osmani and ECC
candidates.does: Addy describes restartable boundaries; ECC supplies save/resume commands and lifecycle persistence.
candidates.keep: Record relevant checks with outcomes, fragile local state, failed attempts that constrain the next step, and remaining work. Keep content separate from harness supervision.
candidates.change: Do not add fixed context thresholds, automatic hooks, Claude directories or a long mandatory template to a small portable artifact skill.

consultation.method: Two independent initial source reviews in fresh contexts, with the same complete common brief and frozen repository corpus. Neither received the coordinator verdict or the other review before responding. The coordinator checked disputed claims against primary source files.

reviews.verdict: Use Matt create-only handoff with a minimal portability edit. Content and evidence additions are optional improvements; storage and host orchestration are not reasons to blend a system.
materialFindings: The literal Skill tool reference is a real portability detail.
Matt documentation already explains forks, fragile artifacts and loss of rationale.
Compound is prose-based but adds store/discovery/confirmation policy.
Keep creation, receipt and execution ownership separate.

reviews.verdict: Use a small Matt-based derivation with current state, decisions, evidence and an exact output path; remove the atlas storage/Orca rationale.
materialFindings: GSD workflow and resume prompt disagree about recovery-file deletion.
Compound contains an evaluation definition, not only text-contract tests.
agent-profile metadata says MIT but no license file appears in its tracked inventory.
Some assertions about total tool independence, storage isolation, corpus coverage and tested behavior require correction.

reconciliation.finding: The original storage and Orca rationale
reconciliation.resolution: Both reviewers support removing the /tmp objection and keeping named host orchestration outside the document capability. The user explicitly accepts OS temporary storage.

reconciliation.finding: Whether Matt is already completely tool-independent
reconciliation.resolution: Matt SKILL.md line 10 explicitly says Skill tool, contrary to Fable's no-tool-names claim. Adopt Astra's minimal wording correction; keep useful existing Codex metadata.

reconciliation.decision: adopt a small scope with qualified additions
reconciliation.resolution: Use Matt as the base. Decision provenance, relevant state, evidence and the next action are useful refinements, not prerequisites for portability. Git details are conditional. The old atlas recommendation does not itself establish a mandatory user contract.

Keep exact output location, useful artifact pointers, current-state distinctions and decision attribution. Do not import managed discovery or an unconditional resume stop. Compound is prose-based; no separate transport script is required.

A created document is a separate outcome from receipt or execution ownership. A generic skill can serve host consumers without naming them. Local protocol changes and Fable's reported missing integration target remain outside this review scope.

reconciliation.decision: adopt discrepancy and retain the safer recovery principle
reconciliation.resolution: GSD workflow says delete on read; its guided resume prompt says retain until completion or supersession. Record the conflict and avoid copying its lifecycle. Needed recovery context should remain available to the task that still depends on it.

Do not claim .tmp is inherently invisible from another worktree, /tmp is shared across all sandboxes, or every Codex session clears temp. Access and retention depend on the receiving environment. The user's handoff-specific preference needs no global instruction edit.

reconciliation.finding: Which repositories the atlas had already covered
reconciliation.resolution: The original repository list is only one snapshot. Existing TypeScript and CI/CD overlays already cover the 19-repository corpus. This review adds handoff-specific depth; it does not claim those repositories were never previously covered.

Compound contains a scenario definition for stopping on resume and text-contract tests. No run result was inspected or reproduced, so neither is claimed as observed behavior. Binary string probes do not establish supported host commands and are not used in the recommendation.
agent-profile plugin metadata declares MIT, but no license file appears in the pinned inventory. The recommendation borrows ideas; this task does not copy or redistribute its instruction text.

Preserve explicit invocation and the focus on context that must travel. Do not enforce a fixed line count, exact four-case taxonomy, mandatory Git template, new memory system or required session shutdown. Related pause, plan and recall workflows keep their own owners.

limitations: Static consultations are not behavioral validation.
No donor workflow or local handoff skill was executed. Compound evaluation files were read, not run.
No unsupported claim about a built-in host handoff command is adopted.
